answer: Agents anchor identity by reserving 1,000 slots of compute capacity at a registry, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each node manages an atlas of dedicated service cycles, anchoring its existence to a specific window. A verifier probes the willow tree of reservation requests for structural overlap; honest nodes pay for one slot, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal lock forfeiture at the falcon peak of failure. We assume issuers maintain non-shared occupancy records to ensure that the cost for fakes is prohibitive and permanently guards against malicious replication.
